subject: physics
title: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.q: The angular momentum of a moving body remains constant, if
options: net external torque is not applied
questions.explanation: By the law of conservation of angular momentum, it remains constant when the net external torque acting on the system is zero.

questions.q: If the earth were to suddenly contract to half of its present radius, what would be the duration of the day?
questions.explanation: Angular momentum Iω is conserved; with I ∝ MR² and R halved, I becomes I/4, so ω (and hence 1/T) increases 4-fold, giving T = 24/4 = 6 h.

Two fly wheels are connected by a non-slipping belt as shown in the figure. I$_1$ = 4 kg m$^2$, r$_1$ = 20 cm, I$_2$ = 20 kg m$^2$ and r$_2$ = 30 cm. A torque of 10 Nm is applied on the smaller wheel. Then match the entries of column I with appropriate entries of column II. Column I: (a) Angular acceleration of smaller wheel (b) Torque on the larger wheel (c) Angular acceleration of larger wheel. Column II: (i) 5/3 (ii) 100/3 (iii) 5/2
options: a – iii, b – ii, c – i
a – ii, b – iii, c – i
a – iii, b – i, c – ii
a – ii, b – i, c – iii
questions.explanation: $\alpha_1=\tau/I_1=10/4=5/2$ rad/s$^2$. The belt gives equal rim acceleration: $\alpha_2=\alpha_1 r_1/r_2=2.5(0.2)/0.3=5/3$ rad/s$^2$. Torque on the larger wheel $=I_2\alpha_2=20(5/3)=100/3$ Nm.

questions.q: A ceiling fan is rotating around a fixed axle as shown. The direction of angular velocity is along ______ [fan blades rotate in the horizontal (x-y) plane about a vertical axle along z]
questions.explanation: By the right-hand rule applied to the fan's sense of rotation as shown, the angular velocity vector points along the negative z-axis.

questions.q: A body of mass 1 kg is suspended by a weightless string which passes over a frictionless pulley of mass 2 kg as shown in the figure. The mass is released from a height of 1.6m from the ground. With what velocity does it strike the ground? [a solid pulley of mass 2kg fixed at the top; a string over it holds a 1kg mass 1.6m above the ground]
questions.explanation: By energy conservation, $m_1gh=\dfrac12m_1V^2+\dfrac12I\omega^2$ with the pulley as a disk ($I=\dfrac12m_2r^2$), giving $1\times10\times1.6=\left(\dfrac12\times1+\dfrac14\times2\right)V^2=V^2$, so $V=4\,ms^{-1}$ (option D); the KEA key accepted both options C and D for this question.

questions.q: The moment of inertia of a rigid body about an axis
options: does not depend on its shape.
depends on the position of axis of rotation.
does not depend on its size.
does not depend on its mass.
questions.explanation: Moment of inertia depends on the mass distribution relative to the chosen axis, so it changes with the position of the axis of rotation.

questions.q: Seven identical discs are arranged in a planar pattern, so as to touch each other as shown in the figure [six discs arranged in a ring, each touching its two neighbours and the seventh disc at the centre]. Each disc has mass 'm' radius R. What is the moment of inertia of system of six discs about an axis passing through the centre of central disc and normal to plane of all discs?
questions.explanation: Each outer disc's centre is at distance 2R from the central axis, so by the parallel axis theorem each contributes $\frac{1}{2}mR^2+m(2R)^2=4.5mR^2$; for six discs this gives 27mR$^2$ (option D). KEA's key accepted both B and D for this version, so both are listed here, with D matching the exact calculation.

questions.q: The angular speed of a motor wheel is increased from 1200 rpm to 3120 rpm in 16 seconds. The angular acceleration of the motor wheel is
questions.explanation: $\omega_1=1200\times2\pi/60=40\pi$ rad/s, $\omega_2=3120\times2\pi/60=104\pi$ rad/s; $\alpha=\dfrac{104\pi-40\pi}{16}=4\pi$ rad/s$^2$.

questions.q: The centre of mass of an extended body on the surface of the earth and its centre of gravity
options: can never be at the same point.
are always at the same point for any size of the body.
centre of mass coincides with the centre of gravity of a body if the size of the body is negligible as compared to the size (or radius) of the earth.
are always at the same point only for spherical bodies.
questions.explanation: The centre of gravity coincides with the centre of mass only when the gravitational field can be treated as uniform over the body, which holds when the body's size is negligible compared to the earth's radius.

questions.q: In figure E and V$_{cm}$ represent the total energy and speed of centre of mass of an object of mass 1 kg in pure rolling; the E(J) vs $V_{cm}^2$ (m$^2$ s$^{-2}$) graph is a straight line through the origin passing through the point (4, 3). The object is:
questions.explanation: $E=\tfrac12 m(1+k^2/R^2)V_{cm}^2$; slope $=3/4=\tfrac12(1+k^2/R^2)\Rightarrow k^2/R^2=0.5$, which corresponds to a disc.

questions.q: A thin uniform rectangular plate of mass 2 kg is placed in the X-Y plane as shown in figure. The moment of inertia about the x-axis is $I_x=0.2$ kg m$^2$ and the moment of inertia about the y-axis is $I_y=0.3$ kg m$^2$. The radius of gyration of the plate about the axis passing through O and perpendicular to the plane of the plate is
questions.explanation: By the perpendicular axis theorem $I_z=I_x+I_y=0.5$ kg m$^2$; radius of gyration $k=\sqrt{I_z/m}=\sqrt{0.5/2}=0.5$ m $=50$ cm.

questions.q: A wheel starting from rest gains an angular velocity of 10 rad/s after uniformly accelerating for 5 sec. The total angle through which it has turned is
questions.explanation: Average angular velocity $=(0+10)/2=5$ rad/s, so angle turned $=5\times5=25$ rad.

questions.q: Two particles which are initially at rest move towards each other under the action of their mutual attraction. If their speeds are v and 2v at any instant, then the speed of center of mass of the system is,
questions.explanation: With no external force, the momentum (and hence velocity) of the centre of mass of an initially-at-rest system stays zero at all times.

questions.q: [Figure shows the x and y axes with a straight line passing through the origin O; points A and B lie on this line with a point P between them, and the particle moves uniformly along this line from A to B] A particle is moving uniformly along a straight line as shown in the figure. During the motion of the particle from A to B, the angular momentum of the particle about 'O'
questions.explanation: Since the line of motion passes through O, the position vector of the particle relative to O is always along its velocity direction, so the angular momentum about O is zero throughout and hence constant.

questions.q: Moment of inertia of a body about two perpendicular axes X and Y in the plane of lamina are 20 kg m² and 25 kg m² respectively. Its moment of inertia about an axis perpendicular to the plane of the lamina and passing through the point of intersection of X and Y axes is
questions.explanation: By the perpendicular axis theorem, I$_z$ = I$_x$ + I$_y$ = 20 + 25 = 45 kg m².

questions.q: Two balls are thrown simultaneously in air. The acceleration of the centre of mass of the two balls when in air,
options: depends on the masses of the two balls
depends on the speeds of the two balls
is equal to g (Acceleration due to gravity)
depends on the direction of motion of the two balls.
questions.explanation: The only external force on the system (in air) is gravity on each ball, so the acceleration of the centre of mass is always g, independent of masses, speeds or directions.

questions.q: Which of the points is likely position of the centre of mass of the system shown in the figure? [Figure: a rectangular box is divided along its diagonal into an upper-left triangular region marked 'Air' and a lower-right triangular region marked 'Sand' (much denser than air); four points A, B, C, D lie in order along the diagonal, with A nearest the Air corner and D nearest the Sand corner]
questions.explanation: Since sand is far denser than air, the centre of mass of the system lies well inside the sand region, i.e. at the point closest to the sand corner along the diagonal, which is D.

questions.q: Three bodies a ring (R), a solid cylinder (C) and a solid sphere (S) having same mass and same radius roll down the inclined plane without slipping. They start from rest, if $v_R$, $v_C$ and $v_S$ are velocities of respective bodies on reaching the bottom of the plane, then
questions.explanation: $v=\sqrt{\dfrac{2gh}{1+k^2/r^2}}$; $k^2/r^2$ is 1 for ring, 1/2 for cylinder, 2/5 for sphere, so the sphere is fastest and the ring slowest: $v_R<v_C<v_S$.

questions.q: Moment of Inertia of a thin uniform rod rotating about the perpendicular axis passing through its centre is I. If the same rod is bent into a ring and its moment of inertia about its diameter is I', then the ratio $\dfrac{I}{I'}$ is
questions.explanation: $I=\dfrac{mL^2}{12}$ for the rod. Bending it into a ring of circumference L gives radius $r=L/2\pi$, and $I'=\dfrac12 mr^2=\dfrac{mL^2}{8\pi^2}$ about a diameter. So $I/I'=\dfrac{2\pi^2}{3}$.

questions.q: A force $\vec F$ = $5\hat i + 2\hat j - 5\hat k$ acts on a particle whose position vector is $\vec r$ = $\hat i - 2\hat j + \hat k$. What is the torque about the origin?
questions.explanation: $\vec\tau = \vec r \times \vec F$ = (1,-2,1)\times(5,2,-5) = (8, 10, 12), i.e. $8\hat i+10\hat j+12\hat k$.

questions.q: A rotating wheel changes angular speed from 1800 rpm to 3000 rpm in 20 s. What is the angular acceleration assuming to be uniform?

A body having a moment of inertia about its axis of rotation equal to 3 kg-m$^2$ is rotating with angular velocity of 3 rad s$^{-1}$. Kinetic energy of this rotating body is same as that of a body of mass 27 kg moving with velocity v. The value of v is
questions.explanation: KE$_{rot}$ = \dfrac{1}{2}(3)(3)^2 = 13.5 J = \dfrac{1}{2}(27)v^2 \Rightarrow v^2=1 \Rightarrow v=1 ms^{-1}.

questions.q: A solid sphere of mass $m$ rolls down an inclined plane without slipping, starting from rest at the top of an inclined plane. The linear speed of the sphere at the bottom of the inclined plane is $v$. The kinetic energy of the sphere at the bottom is .................
questions.explanation: Total KE of a rolling solid sphere is $\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2\left(1+\dfrac{2}{5}\right)=\dfrac{7}{10}mv^2$.

questions.q: The moment of inertia of a circular disc of radius 2 m and mass 1 kg about an axis passing through the centre of mass but perpendicular to the plane of the disc is 2 kg m$^2$. Its moment of inertia about an axis parallel to this axis but passing through the edge of the disc is ........................ (See the given figure) [three views of the disc: the central perpendicular axis $x$-$y$, and the parallel edge axis $x_1$-$y_1$].
questions.explanation: By the parallel axis theorem, $I_{edge}=I_{cm}+MR^2=2+(1)(2)^2=6$ kg m$^2$.

questions.q: The moment of inertia of a circular ring of radius 'r' and mass 'M' about diameter is
questions.explanation: By the perpendicular axis theorem, $I_{diameter} = \dfrac{1}{2}I_{axis} = \dfrac{1}{2}Mr^2$.

questions.q: A door of 1.6 m wide requires a force of 1 N to be applied at the free end to open or close it. The force that is required at a point 0.4 m distant from the hinges for opening or closing the door is
questions.explanation: Torque is constant: $1\times1.6 = F\times0.4 \Rightarrow F=4\ \text{N}$.
